facts.claim: After 24 h of sustained wakefulness and with 0.08%BAC, individuals showed maximal cognitive impairment; however, the magnitude of impairment found for fatigue was equivalent only to that observed for 0.05%BAC.
facts.quote: After 24 h of sustained wakefulness and with 0.08%BAC, individuals showed maximal cognitive impairment; however, the magnitude of impairment found for fatigue was equivalent only to that observed for 0.05%BAC.

facts.claim: Fatigue caused greater impairment than alcohol on the speed of continuous attention and memory and learning, and on the accuracy of complex matching.
facts.quote: It was demonstrated that fatigue caused greater impairment than alcohol on the speed of continuous attention and memory and learning, and on the accuracy of complex matching.

facts.claim: Acute sleep deprivation produced a disproportionate risk to driving safety by selectively and rapidly degrading operational vehicle control compared to cumulative sleep restriction.
facts.quote: cumulative sleep restriction produced only limited changes in driving performance, whereas acute sleep deprivation produced a disproportionate risk to driving safety by selectively and rapidly degrading operational vehicle control.

facts.claim: After 17-19 hours without sleep, performance on some tests was equivalent or worse than that at a BAC of 0.05%.
facts.quote: After 17-19 hours without sleep, corresponding to 2230 and 0100, performance on some tests was equivalent or worse than that at a BAC of 0.05%.

facts.claim: After longer periods without sleep, performance reached levels equivalent to the maximum alcohol dose given to subjects (BAC of 0.1%).
facts.quote: After longer periods without sleep, performance reached levels equivalent to the maximum alcohol dose given to subjects (BAC of 0. 1%).

facts.claim: Approximately 20-25 h of wakefulness produced performance decrements equivalent to those observed at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.10%.
facts.quote: equating the performance impairment in the two conditions indicated that, depending on the task measured, approximately 20-25 h of wakefulness produced performance decrements equivalent to those observed at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0. 10%.

research.angle: While prolonged wakefulness often produces impairments equivalent to moderate alcohol levels, the specific magnitude of that impairment varies significantly depending on the cognitive task and the statistical method used.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that sleep deprivation causes significant cognitive and motor impairments that can match alcohol intoxication, but the severity of these effects is task-dependent and may be overestimated in some studies.
research.caveat: The magnitude of fatigue-related impairment is highly dependent on the specific task measured and the statistical methods used to account for performance variability.
